fact: The RNPP (Registre national des personnes physiques) holds citizens' biometric and civil data and assigns each a national identification number (NNI), with 11 million people holding one according to the ONECI director-general as relayed by the article.

BCPFS and ONECI signed a convention on 2 April 2026 interconnecting the Registre Social Unique with ONECI's databases, so beneficiaries are identified through the Registre National des Personnes Physiques run by ONECI.

ONECI, under the Interior Ministry, is described as managing the RNPP and assigning the national identification number, which is the basis the PARAE feasibility study launched on 5 October 2026 builds on.
ONECI's director general said on 16 September 2025 that its civil-status system and national server are linked to the Registre national des personnes physiques.
ONECI says the Registre National des Personnes Physiques (RNPP) has been instituted and each citizen can now obtain a National Identification Number (NNI) through it.
ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 list the deployment of the RNPP as an operational enabler and name consolidating an integrated national population register as a prospect.
ONECI deputy director general Pélagie Gonto said in October 2024 that identity cards are issued under the project of the national register of natural persons.
Cote d'Ivoire has established the National Register of Natural Persons (RNPP) as a foundational component of its identity infrastructure, managed alongside ONECI's systems.
